resources.string: Speak into any text field, and your psst server writes it down.
Enter the name or address of the machine that runs psst-server, or scan the QR code that psst-server pair prints there.
Run psst-server pair --name phone on the server machine, then scan its QR code or enter the code it prints within 5 minutes.
The link pairs psst with %1$s. Pair if that\'s your server.
The link pairs psst with %1$s, in place of %2$s.
psst records only while you dictate.
Allowed. psst records only while you dictate.
Android no longer asks for it here: open psst\'s settings, then Permissions, and allow the microphone.
Turn psst on in the keyboard settings. Android warns that a keyboard can see what you type; psst only inserts what you dictate.
On. Switch to psst from any text field, or here.

Optional: a button on any keyboard, to dictate with one tap instead of switching keyboards yourself. Android warns that it can see your screen; psst only looks at the field you are in and where the keyboard is.
If Android says it is a restricted setting, open App info, tap ⋮, choose Allow restricted settings, and turn the bubble on again.
On. Tap the bubble on the keyboard to dictate; drag it if it is in the way.
The bubble types your words straight into the field. Where a field doesn\'t allow that, it switches to psst and back as usual.
Tap the field, then the round button, and speak.
Tap the field, switch to psst, tap the round button, and speak.
Tap the field, then the psst bubble on the keyboard, and speak.
